subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Dislocations: Defects That Let Metals Bend
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dislocations: Defects That Let Metals Bend usable.

hook.text: A perfect crystal would be incredibly strong. Real metals bend easily because their lattice has defects called dislocations.

buildup.text: A dislocation is an extra half-plane of atoms jammed into the crystal. Under stress, it glides through the lattice like a ripple.

discovery.text: Moving a dislocation requires far less energy than sliding entire atomic planes at once. Defects make deformation easy.

twist.text: Pile up enough dislocations and they block each other. The metal gets harder. This is work hardening — bending makes it stronger.

climax.text: Metallurgists control dislocations through alloying, heat treatment, and cold working. Controlling defects controls strength.

punchline.text: Perfection would be brittle. Defects let metals bend instead of breaking.

quiz.question: How does work hardening strengthen a metal?
options: It removes all dislocations, creating a perfect crystal structure
Dislocations pile up and block each other, resisting further deformation
It changes the metal's chemical composition through repeated bending
